chapter: Freelancing, Miller and the girls' bands
title: Eddie Durham's All-Star Girls Band and wartime travel
summary: His second girls' band ran separately from the Sweethearts, mixed black and white girls, toured with Treasury Department sign-up, and lent its sleeper bus to others.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, it says later, the -- directed your own band. Did you form one yourself?
Just named it Eddie Durham's All-Star Girls Band.

Instead of the Sweethearts. And I could juggle girls. When I ran out of black girls, I used a lot of white -- I'd get them from everywhere. And then when I'd get through with them, I'd send them to (unintelligible)
or something. And that's the way that was going. When we'd go down South, I'd take the white girls out of the band and put them in this band. I kept them separated all the time.

So the Sweethearts was in the Philippines a long time, the other band was in Canada. Then we got involved into the way. The Treasury Department (unintelligible). Because I had to ________ every six months for (unintelligible). And I was signed up as a bar driver for the Treasury Department for these girls. One day a week for (unintelligible). Then seventh day for ourselves on their gas and their food and their cash.

And I used to let a lot of the bands use our sleeper bus. Run into a band like Hawkins, Erskine Hawkins and all of them. They wouldn't have nowhere to sleep during the way. I'd be coming through and while we was playing, I'd say, well, man, use our sleeping bus. Facilities on that and everything. Big trailer bus.
